passage.text: Thailand is a friendly country, and Thais tend to be patient with foreigners.
passage.reading: ˈtaɪlænd ɪz ə ˈfrɛndli ˈkʌntri, ənd ˈtaɪz ˈtɛnd tə bi ˈpeɪʃənt wɪð ˈfɔːrənərz.

passage.text: But it is a good idea to learn a few dos and don'ts before you visit.
passage.reading: bʌt ɪt ɪz ə ˈɡʊd aɪˈdiːə tə ˈlɜːrn ə ˈfjuː ˈduːz ənd ˈdoʊnts bɪˈfɔːr juː ˈvɪzɪt.

passage.text: When you visit a temple, wear modest clothes that cover your shoulders and knees.
passage.reading: wɛn juː ˈvɪzɪt ə ˈtɛmpəl, ˈwɛr ˈmɑːdɪst ˈkloʊðz ðæt ˈkʌvər jʊr ˈʃoʊldərz ənd ˈniːz.

passage.text: Take off your shoes before you go into a temple building or someone's home.
passage.reading: ˈteɪk ˈɔːf jʊr ˈʃuːz bɪˈfɔːr juː ˈɡoʊ ˈɪntuː ə ˈtɛmpəl ˈbɪldɪŋ ɔːr ˈsʌmwʌnz ˈhoʊm.

passage.text: If someone gives you a wai, it is appropriate to wai back.
passage.reading: ɪf ˈsʌmwʌn ˈɡɪvz juː ə ˈwaɪ, ɪt ɪz əˈproʊpriət tə ˈwaɪ ˈbæk.

passage.text: Be respectful to monks and elderly people.
passage.reading: bi rɪˈspɛktfəl tə ˈmʌŋks ənd ˈɛldərli ˈpiːpəl.

passage.text: Do not touch people on the head, because the head is considered special.
passage.reading: duː ˈnɑːt ˈtʌtʃ ˈpiːpəl ɑːn ðə ˈhɛd, bɪˈkɔːz ðə ˈhɛd ɪz kənˈsɪdərd ˈspɛʃəl.

passage.text: Feet are considered dirty, so pointing at things with your feet is not appropriate.
passage.reading: ˈfiːt ər kənˈsɪdərd ˈdɜːrti, soʊ ˈpɔɪntɪŋ ət ˈθɪŋz wɪð jʊr ˈfiːt ɪz ˈnɑːt əˈproʊpriət.

passage.text: Women are not supposed to touch monks.
passage.reading: ˈwɪmɪn ər ˈnɑːt səˈpoʊst tə ˈtʌtʃ ˈmʌŋks.

passage.text: Also, some gestures that are fine in your country may be rude in Thailand.
passage.reading: ˈɔːlsoʊ, sʌm ˈdʒɛstʃərz ðæt ər ˈfaɪn ɪn jʊr ˈkʌntri meɪ bi ˈruːd ɪn ˈtaɪlænd.

passage.text: If you make a mistake, do not worry.
passage.reading: ɪf juː ˈmeɪk ə mɪˈsteɪk, duː ˈnɑːt ˈwɜːri.

passage.text: Most Thais understand that visitors do not know every custom.
passage.reading: ˈmoʊst ˈtaɪz ˌʌndərˈstænd ðæt ˈvɪzɪtərz duː ˈnɑːt ˈnoʊ ˈɛvri ˈkʌstəm.
ə pəˈlaɪt ˈsɑːri ɪz ˈjuːʒuəli ɪˈnʌf.
